sections.title: God Alone Deserves Worship
sections.body: Tawhid is Islam’s central truth: God is one, incomparable, and alone worthy of worship. It joins belief to a direct way of life—prayer without intermediaries, trust without rivals, and obedience to the Creator rather than creation. Muslims see this same undivided worship in the calls of Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and every prophet.

sections.title: More Than Counting Gods
sections.body:
Tawhid is not merely the statement that only one God exists. It means that the Creator has no partner, child, incarnation, equal, or intermediary who receives a share of worship. God’s knowledge, power, mercy, and authority belong to Him alone.

Its opposite is shirk: directing worship to something created or assigning to creation what belongs uniquely to God. Tawhid therefore changes daily life. A Muslim asks God directly, depends on Him ultimately, repents to Him, and refuses to make wealth, status, desire, or any human being an object of devotion.

sections.title: The Message of Every Prophet
sections.body:
The Quran presents worship of the one God as the shared call of all messengers:

وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدُونِ

“And We sent not before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that, "There is no deity except Me, so worship Me."” (Quran 21:25)

Quran 16:36 gives the same mission across nations: worship Allah and reject false gods. Islam therefore does not claim that Muhammad introduced a new deity. It claims that he restored the undivided worship taught by Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and the prophets between them.

sections.title: The Quran’s Clear Definition
sections.body:
Surah Al-Ikhlas gives the Quran’s shortest complete statement of Tawhid:

بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ

“Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One,” (Quran 112:1)

ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ

“Allah, the Eternal Refuge.” (Quran 112:2)

لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ

“He neither begets nor is born,” (Quran 112:3)

وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌۢ

“Nor is there to Him any equivalent."” (Quran 112:4)

God is one, eternally self-sufficient, neither born nor giving birth, and without equal. Quran 42:11 adds that nothing is like Him. These verses rule out both crude idols and subtler claims that a created being shares God’s identity or right to worship.

sections.title: Moses and Jesus Affirm One God
sections.body:
The Torah’s central confession states:

“Hear, Israel: Yahweh is our God. Yahweh is one.” (Deuteronomy 6:4)

When Jesus is asked for the greatest commandment, he repeats it:

“Jesus answered,
“The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one:” (Mark 12:29)

Isaiah 45:5 likewise declares that there is no God besides the Lord. Muslims see a consistent pattern: the prophets call people to God, pray to God, and never ask to receive God’s worship for themselves.

sections.title: Why Tawhid Differs From the Trinity
sections.body:
Christians affirm one divine being in three coequal persons and insist that this is monotheism. That belief should be stated accurately. Islam’s objection is that the prophets’ clearest creeds do not define God as three persons or identify a human messenger as God incarnate.

Tawhid keeps the distinction found throughout prophetic worship: God sends; the messenger is sent. God answers prayer; the prophet prays. God is worshiped; the prophet teaches people to worship Him. For Muslims, this is not a smaller view of Jesus. It honors him as Messiah and messenger without transferring the Creator’s rights to creation.

sections.title: The Freedom Tawhid Gives
sections.body:
Tawhid frees worship from priests, saints, images, ancestors, and social power. No created being controls forgiveness or blocks access to God. A person may turn directly to the One who knows every hidden fear and every sincere prayer.

It also gives moral courage. If only God is ultimate, no ruler, crowd, appetite, or ideology deserves unconditional obedience. The believer has one final judge and one source of lasting hope.

sections.title: Three Common Misunderstandings
sections.body:
**Allah is not another deity.** Allah means God in Arabic. The disagreement is about how the God of the prophets should be understood, not about a separate creator.

**God’s transcendence does not make Him distant.** The Quran describes Him as merciful, hearing, near, and responsive. Tawhid removes intermediaries rather than removing intimacy.

**Muslims do not worship the Kaaba.** It is a shared direction for prayer. Worship is directed to the Lord of the Kaaba, not the building.

sections.title: One God, One Direct Invitation
sections.body:
Tawhid gathers the prophetic message into one clear commitment: the Creator alone deserves worship. Its strength is both intellectual and spiritual. It gives a coherent account of God without divine partners or incarnation, and it gives every human being direct access to mercy, guidance, and repentance.

Islam begins with this invitation because everything else follows from it: recognize the One who created life, worship Him without partners, and follow the guidance He sent through His messengers.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
**What does Tawhid mean?**
Tawhid means affirming God as absolutely one: He alone creates and sustains, He alone deserves worship, and nothing shares His unique perfection.

**Is Allah a different god?**
No. Allah is the Arabic word for God and is also used by Arabic-speaking Christians. Muslims mean the Creator worshiped by Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, while disagreeing with later doctrines that divide or incarnate the divine identity.

**What is shirk?**
Shirk is giving a created being any share of worship or of God’s exclusive lordship. It includes praying to another being for what only God can grant. Sincere repentance remains open during life.

**Did Jesus teach that God is one?**
Yes. In Mark 12:29, Jesus answers the question about the greatest commandment by repeating the Shema: the Lord is one. Christians read this alongside the Trinity; Muslims understand it in its direct prophetic sense.

sections.title: Further Reading
sections.body:
Selected sources and further reading:

- **The Fundamentals of Tawheed** — Abu Ameenah Bilal Philips. A widely read English introduction to the categories of Tawhid and the forms of shirk.
- **The Creed of Imam al-Tahawi (al-Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah)** — Imam Abu Ja'far al-Tahawi. A classical, broadly accepted summary of Muslim beliefs about God and His attributes.
- **Kitab al-Tawhid** — Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab. A classical thematic work on the oneness of worship and warnings against shirk.
- **The Divine Reality: God, Islam and the Mirage of Atheism** — Hamza Andreas Tzortzis. A contemporary case for God's existence and oneness, useful for readers coming from a secular background.

quranVerses.arabic: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَٰمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُ ٱلْمُهَيْمِنُ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْجَبَّارُ ٱلْمُتَكَبِّرُ ۚ سُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ

quranVerses.arabic: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْخَٰلِقُ ٱلْبَارِئُ ٱلْمُصَوِّرُ ۖ لَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ ۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

quranVerses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَمَن يُشْرِكْ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱفْتَرَىٰٓ إِثْمًا عَظِيمًا
quranVerses.translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.

bibleVerses.text: Hear, Israel: Yahweh is our God. Yahweh is one.

Jesus answered,
“The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one:

I am Yahweh, and there is no one else.
Besides me, there is no God.
I will strengthen you,
though you have not known me;

“I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
“You shall have no other gods before me.
